Question: What is the real name of the free jazz drummer on the album "Center of the World"?
Thought 1: I need to find the real name of the free jazz drummer on the album "Center of the World". I will start by searching for the album "Center of the World".
Action 1: Search[Center of the World (album)]
Observation 1: Center of the World is an album by the Frank Wright Quartet, consisting of saxophonist Frank Wright, pianist Bobby Few, bassist Alan Silva and drummer Muhammad Ali. It was recorded live in 1972 and released on the French Center of the World label.. The album was reissued on CD in 1999 by Fractal with two previously unreleased performances from a 1978 reunion.. In his review for AllMusic, Thom Jurek states "While Wright is the leader of the ensemble and was capable of blowing the hell out of his horn, the true star on these sessions is Few, who joined Steve Lacy's Sextet upon departure from this group."[1]. Writing for Cadence, Derek Taylor called the album "revelatory," offering "undeniable evidence of the Reverend Frank Wright's rightful place in the pantheon of early free Jazz forefathers."[2].
Thought 2: The drummer on the album is Muhammad Ali. I need to find his real name.
Action 2: Search[Muhammad Ali (drummer)]
Observation 2: Muhammad Ali (born Raymond Patterson, December 23, 1936)[1] is an American free jazz drummer.. Ali was born and raised in Philadelphia where he, along with his father and brothers, converted to Islam. His older brother, Rashied Ali, was also a drummer.[2][3]. He recorded with Albert Ayler in 1969 on the sessions released as Music Is the Healing Force of the Universe and The Last Album.[4] Like many Jazz musicians of the 60's, he moved to Europe in 1969 along with Frank Wright, Noah Howard, and Bobby Few.[1]. The Jazz Discography states that Ali participated in 26 recording sessions from 1967 to 1983.[5][6].
Thought 3: The real name of Muhammad Ali (the drummer) is Raymond Patterson.
Action 3: Finish[Raymond Patterson]
